answers.answer: To control who can use a command: open Commands, choose the command on the Channel commands tab, pick the lowest allowed role in Who can use it, and choose Save changes. To control how often: open Trigger and cooldowns, type whole seconds in Chat cooldown (seconds) and/or Per-person cooldown (seconds), and choose Save changes. System commands work the same way but need Customize first.
answers.quote: Pick the lowest role that may use the command, and every role above it can use it too

answers.answer: You need permission to edit commands in this channel. The broadcaster grants it on Permissions, through a team role or the Bot manager capability. It is stated in the opening paragraph.
answers.quote: Changing them needs permission to edit commands in this channel; without it the System commands tab is hidden, and you see only the Channel commands list.

answers.answer: After saving, the unsaved-change count leaves the footer. When the Trigger and cooldowns group is closed, its heading sums up the cooldowns. The two cooldowns differ in scope: the chat cooldown blocks everyone, and the per-person cooldown blocks only the viewer who ran the command.
answers.quote: To see that it saved, close the group: its heading shows what is set, such as “30 s chat · 10 s per person”, or “No cooldown” when both are 0.

answers.answer: Take a chat cooldown of 10 and a per-person cooldown of 60. Viewer B can run the command at second 15 because the chat cooldown ended at 10, and that run restarts the chat cooldown. When viewer A tries again before their own 60 seconds end, A is refused with the cooldown line and neither cooldown restarts. A can run it at second 60 if the chat cooldown has also ended. Both cooldowns must have ended for that viewer.
answers.quote: At second 30, viewer A tries again. A’s own cooldown has 30 seconds left, so the bot sends the cooldown line, and neither cooldown restarts.

answers.answer: Two small guesses, neither blocking. First, the system-command Reset to default flow is prose only: the page says the dialog exists and how to confirm it, and opening it from the footer is only implied. Second, the preset check ends with closing the dialog, but no button is named for that. I also learned only after the role steps that moderator badges skip cooldowns, which matters for testing. The page does point ahead to that from the opening paragraph and the troubleshooting section.

Read aloud, the full eight-role ladder and the per-platform badge mapping make a long run of names. Kick and YouTube members mapping to a role called Twitch subscribers sounds like a mistake when heard, though the page means it literally. Neither is a material obstacle.
answers.quote: the moderator, VIP and subscriber badges are Moderators, VIPs and Twitch subscribers.
